title: Hand Over Mouth Emoji 🫢 Meaning: The Shocked Gasp
description: The hand over mouth emoji 🫢 is a gasp: wide eyes and a hand clapped over the mouth for shock, scandal or “I can't believe you said that.” See how it differs from 🤭.
summary: 🫢 shows a wide-eyed face with a hand clapped over its mouth. It means a gasp. People use it for shock, disbelief, scandalous news, and the moment right after blurting out something they should not have said. It is surprise with a hint of drama.
meaning: The gesture is one everybody recognizes: something shocking happens and a hand flies up to cover an open mouth. 🫢 puts that in a message. It reacts to plot twists, breakups nobody saw coming, a friend's wild confession, or a public figure saying something outrageous. The tone is “oh my god,” and it can be delighted or dismayed depending on the news.

It is also what you send after your own slip. Letting out a secret, swearing in front of a grandparent or sending a screenshot to the person in the screenshot all call for 🫢. Used this way it means “I should not have said that.” The eyes are what make the difference from a giggle: the sender is rattled, at least for show.

Much of its everyday use is theatrical. Online, people gasp at things that are not shocking at all, for comic effect. “You've never seen Shrek? 🫢” treats a harmless fact as a scandal. Fans use it for surprise album drops and casting news, and group chats use it as the standard response to tea, meaning gossip that is being served fresh.

This emoji exists to solve a specific problem. The older 🤭 was being read as a laugh on some phones and as shock on others because vendors drew its eyes differently. 🫢 was approved in 2021 as the unambiguous shocked version, leaving 🤭 to mean the giggle. It reached most phones the following year.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It is mainly a reaction. Someone drops big news and 🫢 comes back, sometimes alone, sometimes with “WAIT” or “no way.” It also follows the sender's own bombshells, as in “I quit today 🫢,” where it acknowledges how big the statement is and invites the other person to react in kind.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Comment sections fill with 🫢 under storytime videos, exposed screenshots, and celebrity news. It is also used for reveals such as haircuts, renovations and pregnancy announcements, where it stands for stunned admiration. Paired with a bold opinion in a caption, it means the poster knows the take will stir people up.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: After a daring or flirty message, 🫢 means “I can't believe you just said that,” usually in a pleased way. It is a reaction, not an advance: the person is showing surprise, and you will need their next message to know whether they liked it. Combined with a laughing or blushing emoji, the answer is yes.

examples.meaning: Real shock at unexpected news about a couple.

examples.text: I just called my boss by my ex's name 🫢
examples.meaning: Mortified at a slip of the tongue the moment it happened.

examples.text: Wait, that was supposed to be a surprise? 🫢
examples.meaning: Realizing too late that a secret was given away.

examples.text: You paid HOW much for those tickets 🫢
She said that to his face 🫢
examples.meaning: Scandalized and entertained by someone's bold comment.
A gasp of admiration at a dramatic change.

combos.meaning: Gossip is being shared and the sender is shocked and eager for more.
Stunned and embarrassed at once, often after seeing or saying something awkward.
The sender just noticed something scandalous and cannot look away.
A secret nearly escaped, and the sender is now sealing their lips.

confusedWith.difference: 🤭 has smiling eyes and hides a giggle, so it suits teasing and playful oops moments. 🫢 has round, startled eyes and hides a gasp. The hand is the same; the eyes tell you whether it is laughter or shock.
😮 shows plain surprise with nothing hidden. 🫢 adds the hand, which implies the thing is scandalous, embarrassing or not supposed to be said out loud. It carries more drama and a sense of secrecy.
😱 grips its face with both hands and screams, for horror or over-the-top panic. 🫢 is quieter: one hand, a held breath, and shock that is more social than frightened.

avoid: Do not reply with it to tragic news, because a theatrical gasp can look like you are treating someone's loss as gossip.
Avoid it when a friend shares something vulnerable and needs acceptance, since it suggests you are scandalized.
Skip it in formal messages, where words like “I'm surprised to hear that” do the job without the drama.
design: A yellow face with wide, round eyes and raised eyebrows, one hand pressed flat over its mouth. It deliberately mirrors the layout of 🤭 with only the eyes changed. Designs are closely aligned across Apple, Google, Samsung and Microsoft. On devices that predate it, the emoji may appear as an empty box or a question mark.

faqs.q: What is the difference between 🫢 and 🤭?
faqs.a: 🫢 is shock and 🤭 is laughter. Both cover the mouth with a hand, but 🫢 has open, alarmed eyes and 🤭 has happy, crinkled ones. Send 🫢 for “no way!” and 🤭 for “hehe, oops.”

Not necessarily. It only says the sender is surprised. The surprise can be thrilled, as with an engagement, or dismayed, as with a firing. The words around it, or the news it replies to, tell you which.

It often is. People use it to fake being scandalized by trivial things, like a friend admitting they dislike pizza. That mock outrage is one of its most common uses, and it is meant to be funny, not judgmental.

faqs.q: Why does 🫢 show up as a box on my phone?
faqs.a: It was approved in 2021 and reached phones in system updates the following year. Devices and apps that have not been updated since then lack the image and display a placeholder square or question mark in its place.
